transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Carlos (AE), Maya (SE), Evelyn (Field Enablement), Priya (CTO roleplay), Samir (Head of ML roleplay), Lena (Procurement roleplay)

Summary:
This was an internal field enablement roleplay where Carlos and Maya ran a sandbox demo targeted at a hypothetical customer, Nimbus Health. Focus areas: messaging for healthcare/PHI, positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI, demo flow (end-to-end search + summarization + reranking), objections: latency vs cost, private deployment and SOC2. We practiced a canary fallback story and a short benchmark ask.

Topics covered:
- Opening discovery: timeline, success criteria, stakeholders [00:02:10]
- Core demo flow: ingest -> embeddings -> semantic search -> summarization + instruction tuning [00:08:20]
- Competitive narrative vs Anthropic/OpenAI/Cohere [00:26:40]
- Deployment options: hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem [00:38:05]
- Security & compliance: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs [00:45:30]
- Pricing and sizing ask for a pilot with 100k daily tokens [00:53:10]
- Recap and next steps [01:03:00]

--- Transcript body (transcription has some errors / filler words, roleplay labels) ---
[00:00:00] Carlos (AE): Okay team, we're on. Hey everyone, this is our Nimbus Health roleplay. Goal for today: nail the 10 minute sandbox demo and rehearse the competitive pushback. Evelyn, you good to run time?
[00:00:10] Evelyn (Enablement): Yep, I got the timer. We'll do a short discovery first, then Maya will demo the sandbox. Priya, Samir, Lena you'll be roleplaying, throw curveballs.
[00:00:22] Priya (CTO roleplay): Sounds good. I'll be direct — low tolerance for latency and heavy audit requirements, ok?
[00:00:30] Carlos: Perfect, let's start with the opening lines. Maya, set the stage: 30 seconds "what we do" for a healthcare ML team.
[00:00:38] Maya (SE): Sure. "Redwood provides a unified inference platform for running LLM workloads — hosted API for rapid pilots, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private deployments for regulated data. Our focus is production economics: predictable latency, cost controls and auditability." (pause) Uh, sorry, that was a mouthful.
[00:01:00] Priya (roleplay): Quick interrupt — what does "production economics" mean in plain terms?
[00:01:07] Carlos: Good point. Maya, short version?
[00:01:10] Maya: It means you get consistent per-token costs, control over batching and caching levers, and clear tradeoffs between latency and cost. Example: with prefix / KV caching we can keep hot workflows under 50ms median for short sequences, while cold starts are still reasonable.
[00:01:28] Samir (roleplay): Wait, K V cache? you mean KV cache — is that at runtime or at the request layer? (small laugh)
[00:01:35] Maya: Sorry, yes KV cache at the runtime level — we keep layers of prefix cache so repeated context doesn't re-run. There was a small mis-say earlier, my fault.
[00:01:45] Lena (procurement roleplay): Okay, processors want to know about encryption at rest. Is customer data stored in your environment during hosted pilots?
[00:01:52] Carlos: Good procurement question. For hosted API we retain transient logs per our default retention, but for PHI you'd want Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and no shared cache with other tenants, Private lets you keep data inside your VPC and integrate your KMS. We'll send SOC 2 and DPA details after the call.
[00:02:10] Evelyn: Noted — call out to add SOC2 link to follow-up.
[00:02:15] (long pause, background typing)
[00:03:05] Carlos: Ok demo time. Maya, please share your screen and walk the sandbox flow. Remember to surface the fallbacks.
[00:03:12] Maya: Sharing. Alright, I'm in the Redwood sandbox project. First step we ingest a small EHR-like CSV, we run a light ETL, generate embeddings using the embeddings endpoint — note the model options (text-embed-large-v2 and a quantized variant) — then we index into the vector store.
[00:03:40] Priya (roleplay): Quick clarification: can you pin model versions? We can't have a floating model change mid-pilot.
[00:03:47] Maya: Yes, you can pin a model version on the route config and we support rollouts — canary, percentage, and instant rollback.
[00:03:55] Samir: How do you measure drift? We need guardrails for model regression when updating.
[00:04:02] Maya: We surface evals tied to prompt sets — you'll get regression alerts for lower ROUGE/accuracy on your golden prompts. Also, quality monitoring can be automated and wired into Slack/webhooks.
[00:04:18] (crosstalk)
[00:04:30] Maya (demo narrating): Now I'll run a sample semantic search: query about "post-op follow-up plan for diabetic patients" — search returns top 5 candidates, then we use the generation route with instruction tuning to summarize and highlight action items.
[00:04:48] Priya (roleplay): How do you avoid hallucinations on clinical suggestions?
[00:04:53] Maya: There are a couple levers — you can bias towards retrieved doc context, increase retrieval size, or use reranking to prefer higher-confidence passages. We also recommend human-in-the-loop for first 10k queries.
[00:05:10] Carlos: Pause there — Evelyn, note that the hallucination story needs a concrete example next time, maybe show a before/after reranking effect.
[00:05:18] Evelyn: Will do.
[00:05:22] Maya: Continuing demo — here's a small snippet where we chain a retrieval + generate call. Oops, the transcript shows a slight lag — you'll see token streaming start after 800ms.
[00:05:35] Samir (roleplay): 800 miliseconds? That's too slow for our UI. We need sub-200ms tails for microinteractions.
[00:05:42] Maya: Understood. For microinteractions we recommend smaller context windows and using a tuned smaller model on Redwood Dedicated. Also intelligent batching can keep cost low without adding latency on single-user flows. There is always a tradeoff.
[00:05:55] Carlos: This is a typical objection — practice the line: "If you need <200ms, we recommend product X in Dedicated with device-local KV caching and a tuned 8-bit quantized model; we can run a microbenchmark in your env."
[00:06:12] Priya (roleplay): And the cost delta?
[00:06:15] Maya: We'll give ballpark numbers in the benchmark proposal; directive: show cost per 1M tokens for the small tuned variant vs the larger baseline.
[00:06:24] (Typing)
[00:06:40] Carlos: Ok switching to the competitive narrative. Evelyn, start the prompt: "How do we position against Anthropic?"
[00:06:47] Evelyn: Right. Anthropic has a safety-first message; we lean in on production economics and the ops story. Example phrasing: "Anthropic is focused on the model; Redwood is focused on serving — we give you consistent latency, cost controls, and deployment modes that match healthcare requirements."
[00:07:05] Maya: Also call out our rollout policies, canary + automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity strains, that tends to resonate with infra teams. Use the word fallback policy, not graceful degrade — folks misunderstand it.
[00:07:20] Samir (roleplay): What about OpenAI? They have great model performance, though we worry about audit logs and enterprise controls.
[00:07:28] Carlos: Positioning vs OpenAI: acknowledge model differences, then pivot to controls — "If your priority is strict audit + private networking + KMS managed keys, Redwood Private gives a customer-managed plane with the same developer API you saw in the sandbox."
[00:07:42] Lena (procurement roleplay): Do you have an HSM/KMS integration list? We need compatible providers listed.
[00:07:48] Maya: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM partners — we'll drop the compatibility matrix in the follow-up.
[00:07:55] (small pause)
[00:08:05] Carlos: Good. Now push on procurement asks — show the procurement compromise: shorter pilot with dedicated commit vs longer enterprise contract. Roleplay Lena asks for discounting.
[00:08:14] Lena (roleplay): You're expensive. Can we get a 30% pilot discount?
[00:08:20] Carlos: For pilots we usually offer usage credits and a short reserved capacity window; encourage offering a pilot-only credit + agreed success criteria to convert. Evelyn, mark that negotiation tactic.
[00:08:30] Evelyn: Noted.
[00:08:35] (transition — Maya demos a gulf benchmark spreadsheet)
[00:08:40] Maya: Here's a quick benchmark spreadsheet link (internal): https://drive.internal/redwood/benchmarks/nimbus-sample (note: roleplay link). We run microbenchmarks: p50, p95 latencies, token throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:08:58] Priya (roleplay): We'll expect a realistic dataset; don't use synthetic prompts only.
[00:09:03] Maya: Agreed — propose using a stripped and de-identified sample EHR extract for the benchmark run. We'll provide an env recipe to run this in your VPC or in our dedicated pilot env.
[00:09:15] Samir (roleplay): How do you route requests? We have multi-region concerns.
[00:09:20] Maya: Smart routing by policy — you can route by latency, cost, or region, with automated fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained. Say: "we can pin region and fallback to another region only if you permit cross-region failover."
[00:09:36] (crosstalk, someone murmurs)
[00:09:50] Carlos: Time check — we've got about 45 minutes left; switch to objections practice. Evelyn, toss in a security late-stage question.
[00:09:58] Evelyn: Alright, Priya, suppose an auditor asks for raw request/response logs for three months. How do we handle that?
[00:10:05] Priya (roleplay): Yeah, we need immutable audit records for compliance.
[00:10:08] Maya: For Private deployments you can persist logs into your S3 and integrate with SIEM. For Dedicated, we can provide extended retention as an add-on; note that hosted default retention is shorter and needs DPA tweaks. Also point out RBAC and per-route access controls in the Console.
[00:10:24] Samir: Any chances of data crossover between tenants on hosted?
[00:10:28] Maya: No data mixing, but compute and caches are multi-tenant on hosted; if strict isolation is required pick Dedicated or Private. There was a slight mis-say earlier on isolation semantics — call it out next time.
[00:10:40] Carlos: Good coaching note.
[00:10:43] (brief silence)
[00:11:05] Priya (roleplay): One last thing — who owns PII redaction in the pipeline?
[00:11:09] Maya: We recommend redaction in your pre-ingest ETL. Redwood can provide helper libraries and plugins to scrub PII before embedding. We'll show a snippet in the next rehearsal.
[00:11:20] Evelyn: Action: add PII redaction snippet to the demo appendix.
[00:11:26] Carlos: Nice. Let's do a lightning run of the opening 90 seconds. Maya, start again.
[00:11:30] Maya (SE): "Hi, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference. We help teams run LLMs reliably across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, with focus on latency, cost, and compliance..." (small stumble)
[00:11:43] Priya (roleplay): Shorten to 30 seconds, include the word "audit" up front.
[00:11:47] Maya: Good call. "...and with first-class audit logs and KMS integrations for regulated workloads."
[00:11:55] Carlos: That was cleaner. Evelyn, mark the 30 second script in the deck.
[00:12:02] (fast forward — later in call)
[00:26:40] (we jump forward in transcript to competitive section, more coaching)
[00:26:45] Carlos: Practice how to answer the "model quality" slam. Maya?
[00:26:50] Maya: "We don't claim a particular model monopoly — instead we offer verified model profiles and performance matrices for recommended models, and we help you choose a quantized variant for cost-sensitive workloads while maintaining output fidelity via eval sets." (stumbles on quantized)
[00:27:05] Priya (roleplay): Do you support custom model uploads?
[00:27:08] Maya: Yes, on Private you can bring your own model artifacts; Dedicated we can host vetted custom models in a customer-dedicated cluster.
[00:27:15] Samir: And versioning?
[00:27:17] Maya: We support model versioning and rollouts in the Console, plus a config layer to pin model versions per route.
[00:27:25] (ambient keyboard sounds)
[00:32:10] (middle of call, benchmark debate)
[00:32:12] Priya (roleplay): If we run a 72-hour pilot, what's realistic throughput?
[00:32:18] Maya: Depends on model/seq length. For a tuned small model we can do tens of thousands of tokens per GPU per second, but the practical number depends on concurrency patterns and batching. We'll propose a conservative throughput target in the benchmark doc.
[00:32:35] Carlos: Coach the phrasing: "We'll propose a realistic SLO (p50/p95) based on your sample traffic; if you want hard p50 <200ms we will run a microbenchmark and produce a hard number."
[00:32:47] Evelyn: I'm noting the SLO phrasing.
[00:32:52] (later)
[00:38:05] (Deployment options discussion)
[00:38:08] Maya: Distinguish Dedicated vs Private: Dedicated is our hosted reserved capacity — predictable throughput and tenant isolation; Private is customer-managed control plane deployed in your VPC or on-prem with direct KMS integration.
[00:38:22] Priya (roleplay): On Private, who manages upgrades?
[00:38:25] Maya: You manage the control plane upgrades or we can operate under a managed services arrangement for major upgrades. For critical workloads we recommend a scheduled maintenance window and a rollback plan.
[00:38:40] Lena (procurement): Any SLA on latency?
[00:38:43] Carlos: We can commit to throughput/uptime SLAs on Dedicated under enterprise agreements — specifics depend on size of committed capacity.
[00:38:52] (note: slight mispronunciation of 'throughput' earlier as 'through-pull')
[00:45:30] (Security review section)
[00:45:32] Maya: Security quick bullets: SOC 2 Type 2, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC per-team, audit logs per-token, KMS integrations, optional VPC peering for Private, and compliance worksheet in the fight deck.
[00:45:49] Priya (roleplay): Who signs the DPA? Our legal needs specific language on sub-processors.
[00:45:55] Carlos: Legal team handles that — we have a standard DPA and addendums for specific regions. We'll attach the DPA PDF in the follow-up.
[00:46:05] (slight overlap as someone speaks)
[00:50:00] (pricing ask)
[00:50:05] Carlos: For the pilot ask: 100k daily tokens, 30 days. Ballpark pricing example was provided during roleplay: hosted credits for the first month, then convert to Dedicated reserve. We'll refine numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:53:10] (pilot scoping)
[00:53:12] Maya: If we run the pilot we'll need sample EHR snippet, expected QPS, and success criteria (accuracy on golden prompts, p95 latency target, and throughput).
[00:53:25] Priya (roleplay): Put these three success criteria in writing.
[00:53:29] Carlos: Yep, that's in the next steps.
[00:54:40] (closing / recap)
[01:03:00] Carlos: Quick recap — agreed next steps: share recording + demo deck, send SOC2/DPA, propose benchmark plan and schedule pilot. Any other asks?
[01:03:12] Priya (roleplay): No, that covers it. Good run.
[01:03:18] Evelyn: Nice job everyone. We'll do another run next week focusing on rapid-fire procurement pushes.
[01:03:25] Carlos: Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.

References/links mentioned:
- Internal benchmark sheet (roleplay): https://drive.internal/redwood/benchmarks/nimbus-sample
- Security artifacts (to be attached) 
- Competitor battlecard (internal doc)

Coaching notes (internal):
- Replace "graceful degrade" with "fallback policy" when speaking to infra
- Use concrete before/after for reranking to show hallucination reduction
- Prep a 30-second opening that mentions audit logs and KMS for regulated buyers
- Bring PII redaction snippet into demo appendix
- Keep the microbenchmark pledge: "we will run a microbenchmark with your de-id sample and return p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens"

End of transcript.
